CONFINED DEPOSITION FEEDBACK: SCIENTIFIC CHECKPOINT
24 October 2026

Problem and positive construction

The selected missing capability is suppressing geometry-driven electrodeposition
roughening without assuming a flat interface or a nanoscale observation/control
oracle. Fixed positive conductivity grading alone preserves long-wave focusing.
A compacting porous interlayer can increase ionic resistance at a protrusion;
a continuous ionic skin is needed so metal does not simply enter the pores.
Pressure-induced pore closure already belongs to Zhang2019; no priority claim
is made for that mechanism. The owned work has become a coupled transport/load
framework and paid design envelope, rather than a new material claim.

The load path is now derived instead of setting the two skin faces equal. For
an explicitly unstressed isotropic plane-strain skin with shear-free faces, its
normal two-port has eigenvalues

 k+=q/[2c_e](tanh l-l sech²l),
 k-=q/[2c_e](coth l+l csch²l),
 l=qb/2, c_e=(1-v_p²)/E.

For a=(k++k-)/2, c=(k+-k-)/2 and skeleton tangent K_w,
m=v_top/h=-c/(a+K_w) and k_eff=a-c²/(a+K_w). Thus 0<m<1; high-q motion no
longer compresses the distant pores, while the film develops half-space stiffness
E q/[2(1-v_p²)]. This avoids extrapolating a thin-plate q^4 law to infinity.

For fixed Eulerian ionic coefficients, the exact linear moving-face numerator is

 N_frozen=(G-chi)(C+LpS)-m(G+j0R_v),
 chi=Gamma q²+nu_m k_eff, G=j0/k_n,
 C=cosh(qb sqrt(rho)), S=sinh(qb sqrt(rho)),
 p=q sqrt(k_n k_t), rho=k_t/k_n,
 D=rC+S/p+L(C+rpS)>0,  delta j/h=N/D.

The skeleton's ionic derivative R_v and its conservative restoring K_w are both
included and both retained by the identical-skin comparator.

Material rotation corrected the first comparison

For a physical tensor with strain-independent intrinsic eigenvalues whose axes
rotate with the skin, the ionic ODE has a first-order distributed source.
The elastic rotation amplitude Rrot is harmonic, with endpoints1,m. The exact
particular potential -G Rrot cancels the moving-face base-field shifts. Hence

 N_rot=-chi(C+LpS)-j0mR_v
       -j0[(S/p+LC)Rrot'(0)-L Rrot'(b)],
 Rrot'(0)=q[m-cosh(qb)]/sinh(qb),
 Rrot'(b)=q[m cosh(qb)-1]/sinh(qb).

For rho>=1 a positive Green-kernel argument proves N_rot<=N_frozen. The old

MATERIAL-AXIS ROTATION, THE STRONGER ORDINARY COATING, AND THE PAID GAIN
Owned continuation of ELASTIC_INTERFACE.txt, 24 October 2026

Scientific change

Whole review exposed a load-bearing constitutive premise in the anisotropic
frozen-coefficient interface. A real crystalline skin can rotate its conductivity
axes as it bends. This note derives that different operator and repeats the
same-skin comparison. The frozen-axis all-q theorem remains a valid theorem for
its stated model; its positive ordinary-skin witness is not evidence that the
stronger rotating ordinary coating is unstable. Original proof/replay files are
preserved. No material or physical cell was acquired by either calculation.

1. Rotation-only constitutive law and exact moving-interface response

Retain the unstressed, shear-free, isotropic elastic two-port of E1--E2.
The ionic tensor has intrinsic eigenvalues k_t,k_n independent of strain, and
rotates by the material's infinitesimal rotation. This is a physical constitutive
assumption, distinct from assigning a fixed Eulerian tensor or a Piola-transformed
reference conductivity. The loaded tangent and strain-dependent intrinsic
conductivity of the actual film remain unacquired.

For a mode exp(i q x), write the horizontal displacement as i U(z) and vertical
displacement as w(z), w(0)=h, w(b)=m h. The infinitesimal rotation in the ordered
(x,z) coordinates is theta=i(qw-U')/2. Rotation of diag(k_t,k_n) gives

 delta k_xz=(k_t-k_n)theta.

Linearizing divergence of electrochemical current about the base gradient
G=j0/k_n therefore gives

 k_n phi''-k_t q^2 phi
       =G(k_t-k_n)q(qw-U')/2.                            (C1)

This source is first order in h. It cannot be removed by calling the conductor
quasistatic. The curl of the homogeneous isotropic Navier equation is harmonic.
With zero shear traction, U'+qw=0 on both faces. Thus

 Rrot(z)=(qw-U')/(2q h)
       =[sinh(q(b-z))+m sinh(qz)]/sinh(qb)>0,             (C2)

Rrot(0)=1 and Rrot(b)=m. Define phi_p=-G Rrot h. Because Rrot''=q^2 Rrot,
this is an exact particular solution of C1, for any k_t/k_n (including the
degenerate isotropic case where it is simply a homogeneous solution).

Let psi=phi+G Rrot h. It satisfies the homogeneous ionic ODE, while its physical
boundary potentials and currents are

 psi(0)=r j_b+chi h,  psi(b)=W,
 j_b=k_n psi'(0)-j0 Rrot'(0)h,
 j_t=k_n psi'(b)-j0 Rrot'(b)h,

ELASTIC IONIC SKIN AND COMPACTING INTERLAYER
Owned physical continuation, 24 October 2026

The operation being constructed is one-stroke suppression and leveling of metal
deposition roughness by a local increase of ionic resistance, while a continuous
solid ionic skin prevents deposition from simply entering the membrane pores.
The ordinary identical skin and mechanical support get the same properties.
This is a conditional coupled-interface construction, not an acquired lithium
cell or a claim of priority over pressure-dependent pore closure.

1. Why both conductivity and mechanics have to be kept

SPREADING_SKIN.txt derived the exact ionic transfer when the two skin faces move
by the same h. A bending film cannot be treated as a plate with stiffness B q^4
at arbitrarily large q b, nor do its two faces necessarily move identically.
This note removes those two assumptions within linear isotropic elasticity.
It also records the separate finite-amplitude column limit precisely.

Let b be the flat skin thickness, k_n,k_t its normal/tangential ionic
conductivities, j0>0 the mean deposition current, and r>=0 the differential
charge-transfer resistance. The skin has no electronic leakage. Concentration
polarization and electrochemical side reactions are excluded from this model.
Potentials below are electrochemical driving potentials; a separately counted
conservative mechanical energy is not counted again as an arbitrary pressure
shift. Write nu_m=Omega_m/(z F)>0 for deposited metal height per areal charge.

The bottom-face displacement is h, top-face displacement v. Above the skin is
a locally confined porous skeleton with fixed upper backing. Its compression is
controlled by v, not automatically by h. At the flat state its ionic resistance
and derivative are R>0 and R_v; its tangent normal mechanical foundation is K_w.
The remaining electrolyte has Fourier impedance Z_b(q)>0. L(q)=R+Z_b(q).
